notes: GH #266 reconciler-framework improvements. Requirements SSOT: docs/product/architecture/adr-0081-reconciler-cadence-and-interest-declarations.md (the LOCKED surface — build ONLY this API, do not invent), docs/feature/reconciler-framework-improvements/feature-delta.md (SYSTEM+APPLICATION), distill/test-scenarios.md (S-266-01..22), design/wave-decisions.md.

Two additive, object-safe, default-provided Reconciler methods. Piece A: resync_schedule(&self) -> Option<ResyncSchedule> (default None). Piece B: interests(&self) -> &'static [Interest] (default &[]). Each returns a CONCRETE type (no associated types) → one AnyReconciler forwarding arm apiece; neither touches AnyState/AnyReconcilerView/the reconcile-dispatch triple-match. NO erasure rework. ADR-0036 stands (hydration stays runtime-owned, per-tick from the CR-SQLite replica; no warm cache — RN-2 = B-2). RN-2=B-2, Open Question 5 resolved, RN-1 locked; do not reopen. Deferrals: GH #270 (B-1 warm cache), GH #271 (Action::EnqueueEvaluation → interests migration), GH #272 (Facet-2 hydration-erasure rework).

TEST PARADIGM (Rust, per .claude/rules/testing.md — OVERRIDES any Python/Hypothesis default). Tier-1 DST is PRIMARY for timing/ordering/concurrency/convergence (Sim* traits, assert_eventually!/assert_always!, seed-reproducible, default lane). proptest for pure functions (resolve_scope, derive_target/TargetFrom::Workload). parametrize/table for classify (closed 8-variant enumeration, NOT PBT — the falsifier gate). Trait signature/purity guards are compile-time/unit. Integration/E2E stay single-example (wiring, not invariants). RED-scaffold: test-side #[should_panic(expected = "RED scaffold")] with panic!("Not yet implemented -- RED scaffold (S-266-NN / ...)"); production-side todo!("RED scaffold: ...") + #[expect(clippy::todo, reason = "RED scaffold; lands GREEN in step <id>")]. NO .feature files, NO Python, NO NotImplementedError.

Every scenario maps to EXACTLY one step and appears in that step's criteria (traceability): 01-01 = {S-266-06, S-266-07}; 01-02 = {S-266-02, S-266-03, S-266-04, S-266-05, S-266-19}; 02-01 = {S-266-11, S-266-17, S-266-21}; 02-02 = {S-266-01, S-266-08, S-266-09, S-266-12, S-266-14, S-266-15, S-266-16, S-266-22}; 02-03 = {S-266-10, S-266-13, S-266-18, S-266-20}. All 22 covered; each once. S-266-06 (resync_schedule purity) is Piece A → 01-01; S-266-17 (interests purity) is Piece B → 02-01. S-266-09/S-266-12 require the live router → placed in 02-02 (router-behavior scenarios) though not enumerated verbatim in the dispatch brief's 02-02 list. The former single S-266-19 conflated a resync + fan-out collapse at ONE broker key — internally unsatisfiable, since ResyncScope::LocalNode resolves to node/n while fan-out derives workload/W, keys that can never collide — so DISTILL SPLIT it into two realizable coalescing scenarios: S-266-19 owns the resync-side same-key collapse (node/n key) at 01-02, and its sibling S-266-22 owns the fan-out write-flood collapse (workload/W key) through the live router at 02-02. Both route through the SAME broker LWW key-collapse (mutation surface #5), pinned separately on each path because a node/… resync key and a workload/… fan-out key never share a broker key.

Execution discipline. Tests run via LIMA ONLY: cargo xtask lima run -- cargo nextest run ...; compile-check cargo xtask lima run -- cargo check --all-targets --features integration-tests. --no-run is NOT a gate (it compiles but runs nothing; a boot-path step must actually RUN the fixtures). Per-step mutation gate ≥80% diff-scoped: cargo xtask mutants --diff origin/main --package <crate> --file <files>, run background (run_in_background: true), on macOS prefixed with cargo xtask lima run -- WHEN --features integration-tests participates. resync_schedule/interests are const-returning bodies → cargo-mutants may generate few/no mutants; criterion coverage then rests on S-266-06/07/11/17/21 asserting the returned data + the routing/loop tests asserting its consumption. Each step is RED (scaffold + failing DST/unit) → GREEN (implement to ADR-0081) → COMMIT (mutation gate + Lima run). Log phases via python3 -m des.cli.log_phase; never edit execution-log.json directly.

Vertical-slice rule (02-02): the router step MUST prove the PRODUCTION entry run_server_with_obs_and_driver (lib.rs:1447) SPAWNS spawn_interest_router — a structural/boot check the router task is live after the entry returns — never a hand-assembled harness and never a hand-call of the spawn fn (honours 'no test installs the one production call site the feature omitted').

Single-cut greenfield migration (02-03): DELETE the four exit_observer submits AND ADD the four interests() overrides in ONE commit, with the pre-existing exit_observer 'enqueues bridge/service/svid' tests rewritten to fan-out equivalence in the SAME commit (deletion discipline). No shim, no deprecation, no feature-flagged old path. Do NOT amend ADR-0036; do NOT invent API beyond ADR-0081.

Roadmap-validator length warnings (STEP_NAME_TOO_LONG / CRITERIA_TOO_LONG / DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG) are cosmetic and non-blocking per CLAUDE.md; ACs deliberately carry scenario ids, invariant names (fixpoint, no-storm, determinism), proptest/parametrize targets, and mutation targets verbatim. Do NOT trim AC specificity for length.

The per-step `criteria` array IS the acceptance-criteria list (the skeleton's AC slot); `test_file`/`scenario_name` name the primary test artifact + scenario ids; `description`, `estimated_hours`, `dependencies`, `implementation_scope`, `implementation_notes` are the added content fields. effort/estimated_hours are advisory only — do not size or defer by budget.

steps.name: Piece A loop wiring — spawn_convergence_loop next-wake table drives resync via broker.submit once per period (delete the cadence/target hardcode)
steps.description: Wire Piece A into the production convergence loop (overdrive-control-plane/src/lib.rs, spawn_convergence_loop :2427; loop owns the injected Clock via clock.now()/clock.sleep(cadence)). At registration build a per-reconciler cadence table BTreeMap<ReconcilerName, UnixInstant> (BTreeMap per development.md ordered-collection rule) from AnyReconciler::resync_schedule() for every reconciler returning Some. Each loop iteration, for any reconciler whose next_wake <= clock.now(): call the core resolve_scope(schedule.scope, &node_id) (node_id owned by the loop — state.node_id :233 / NodeId::new("local") :1701) and broker.submit(Evaluation { reconciler, target }) per resolved target (C-A1: route every resync through broker.submit — the coalescing path — never a side channel), then re-arm next_wake += period (C-A2: at most once per period, never per-tick). DELETE any reconciler-name / cadence-constant / hardcoded-target-scheme from the loop — after this change the loop carries only the generic table + a total scope resolver it calls (pre-empts the incoming VM_RECLAMATION_SWEEP_INTERVAL + node/<id> hardcode; none on main today). No warm cache; hydration stays per-tick from the replica (ADR-0036 stands). No API beyond ADR-0081.
criteria: S-266-02 (@dst @property @contract-shape:bounded-change) — R declares resync_schedule() = Some(ResyncSchedule { period: P, scope: LocalNode }), loop owns local NodeId = n; after SimClock advances k whole periods with no row changes, the broker receives EXACTLY k submits of (R, node/n) — one per period, routed through broker.submit. In-broker count teeth (positive, falsifiable for C-A1): a side-channel bypass makes the in-broker count < k (miss); a per-tick re-arm makes it > k (overshoot); only routing every resync through broker.submit exactly once per period yields k. proptest over P, k, n.

S-266-03 (@dst @property @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — R armed at t0 with period P (next_wake = t0+P): SimClock at t0+P−ε → NO (R, node/n) submit; at t0+P → EXACTLY one; at t0+2P → one more; never one-per-tick within a period. Mutation targets: the next_wake <= now decision (swap <= ↔ <) and the next_wake += period re-arm (drop it) → both caught. C-A2 / no-storm boundary.

S-266-04 (@dst @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — R uses the default resync_schedule() (None): over many periods under SimClock the broker receives ZERO resync-origin submits for R (no cadence table entry is built for R). assert_always no (R, *) submit whose origin is the cadence path. SD-6 (None ⟺ host-backed ⟺ resync-only).

S-266-05 (@dst @property @contract-shape:bounded-change) — X = Some { period: 10s, LocalNode }, Y = Some { period: 30s, LocalNode }, local NodeId = n; over 60s with no row changes X receives 6 submits of (X, node/n) and Y receives 2 of (Y, node/n), each driven purely from its declaration. Companion structural check (DELIVER reviewer, CM-style): a source scan confirms the loop names NO reconciler and NO cadence constant — the loop carries no reconciler name, no cadence constant, no hardcoded target scheme (mirrors eval_broker_does_not_import_clock_transport_entropy).

S-266-19 (@dst @property @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — no resync-storm, resync-on-resync same-key collapse (resync side ONLY): given R declares resync_schedule() = Some(ResyncSchedule { period: P, scope: LocalNode }) with the loop's local NodeId = n and a prior eval already pending at the resync key (R, node/n) (an earlier resync fire, or a same-key self-re-enqueue submit, not yet drained), a redundant same-key resync submit for (R, node/n) while that prior eval is still pending coalesces through the broker's LWW key-collapse to EXACTLY ≤1 pending eval at (R, node/n), and broker.counters.cancelled for the (R, node/n) key increases by EXACTLY 1 — never fewer (a missed collapse) and never more (a double-count). assert_always broker.pending_keys holds ≤1 entry for (R, node/n). C-A1 (broker.submit) + C-A2 (≤1 re-arm/period) keep Open-Question-5's no-storm verdict true on the resync side. Mutation target: broker LWW #5 (resync path) — the LWW key-collapse on (ReconcilerName, TargetResource) the resync submit routes through, exercised at the node/n key. The fan-out write-flood collapse (the workload/W key) is the sibling S-266-22 at 02-02 — a node/… resync key and a workload/… fan-out key can never share a broker key, so the two coalescing paths are asserted separately.

The next-wake table is loop-owned mutable state; the resync_schedule hook stays pure; reconcile is unchanged; ADR-0036 stands (hydration per-tick from the replica, no warm cache). No API beyond ADR-0081; dst-lint clean.

steps.name: Piece B interest-router + run_server vertical slice — spawn_interest_router (List-then-Watch) wired into run_server_with_obs_and_driver
steps.description: Implement spawn_interest_router in overdrive-control-plane/src/lib.rs as List-then-Watch over the EXISTING ObservationStore::subscribe_all_events() (observation_store.rs:1896; NO new port method). Order (ADR-0081 §5): (1) SUBSCRIBE first (a tokio::broadcast subscriber does not see pre-subscription sends — this closes the boot-window gap); (2) LIST the interested snapshot families (alloc_status_rows()) and broker.submit per row's derived target (so an interested reconciler wakes without waiting for a change); (3) WATCH — on SubscriptionEvent::Row(row) call core classify(&row); for each Some(kind) and each interested (reconciler, target_from) in the boot-built interest table BTreeMap<RowKind, Vec<(ReconcilerName, TargetFrom)>> (from AnyReconciler::interests() at registration), derive the TargetResource via core derive_target(...) and broker.submit; on SubscriptionEvent::Lagged { missed } RELIST (repeat step 2 — honours the mandatory Lagged contract, observation_store.rs:1734; no warm cache to rebuild under B-2). The watcher emits a Row only for an ACCEPTED write (LWW winner), so the fan-out fires on genuine changes only. Wire the spawn into the PRODUCTION entry run_server_with_obs_and_driver (lib.rs:1447), alongside the existing convergence-loop spawn (lib.rs:2315). Hydration stays per-tick (ADR-0036, no warm cache). Router's only effect universe is broker.submit; injected capability is a restricted EvaluationBroker handle. No API beyond ADR-0081. This step does NOT yet delete the exit_observer submits or add the 4 real consumers' interests() (that single cut is 02-03); the router-behavior scenarios here use test reconciler fixtures declaring interests.
criteria: S-266-01 (@walking_skeleton @dst @piece-a @piece-b @contract-shape:bounded-change) — VERTICAL SLICE: the runtime is booted through its PRODUCTION composition entry run_server_with_obs_and_driver (lib.rs:1447 — the same entry that spawns the convergence loop at lib.rs:2315) with Sim obs + SimClock, and that entry — NOT the test — spawns spawn_interest_router. Spawn-wiring teeth: the assertion is *does run_server_with_obs_and_driver spawn the router?* (a structural/boot check that the router task is live after the production entry returns), NOT *does the spawn fn exist / compose with the loop?*. The test hand-calls NO spawn fn and hand-assembles NO router (honours the vertical-slice rule: no test installs the one production call site the feature omitted). Primary lane: Tier-1 DST booting the production entry with Sim adapters; fallback: a full run_server Lima boot under integration-tests.

S-266-12 (@dst @piece-b @property @contract-shape:bounded-change) — for an accepted alloc_status row for workload W and an interested (R, TargetFrom::Workload), the router derives TargetResource == workload/<W> and submits (R, workload/W). S-266-14 (@dst @piece-b @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — on SubscriptionEvent::Lagged { missed } mid-stream (rows dropped) the router RELISTS the interested snapshot family (alloc_status_rows()) and re-submits per derived target — every interested target present in the snapshot is woken after the gap (no permanently-missed row). assert_eventually post-Lagged that every snapshot workload target has a submit. S-266-15 (@dst @piece-b @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — List-then-Watch: pre-existing alloc_status rows (written BEFORE the router subscribes) each yield a submit (an interested reconciler wakes without needing a subsequent change), AND no accepted write in the subscribe→list boot window is missed (subscribe FIRST). assert_eventually a submit per snapshot workload target; assert_always no missed boot-window write. C3 count 0/1/many + boot-window edge.

S-266-16 (@dst @piece-b @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — a non-accepted (LWW-loser / no-op) alloc_status write (the watcher never delivers it as a Row) → the router submits NOTHING (fires on genuine accepted changes only, matching the exit-observer's nudge-only-on-change gate). assert_always no submit for a non-delivered write.

S-266-22 (@dst @property @piece-b @error @contract-shape:bounded-change) — no fan-out storm, write-flood collapse (fan-out side), through the LIVE router: given R declares interests() = [Interest { row_kind: AllocStatus, target_from: Workload }] for workload W driven by the live spawn_interest_router → broker.submit, when N accepted alloc_status writes for the same workload W arrive so the router submits N times at the same key (R, workload/W) before the broker drains, the broker collapses to EXACTLY ≤1 pending eval at (R, workload/W) per drain and broker.counters.cancelled for the (R, workload/W) key increases by EXACTLY N−1 — never fewer (a missed collapse) and never more (a double-count). Exercised through the live router (not a hand-fed broker). assert_always broker.pending_keys holds ≤1 entry for (R, workload/W) per drain. Mutation target: broker LWW #5 (fan-out path) — the SAME LWW key-collapse on (ReconcilerName, TargetResource) the resync path routes through at 01-02, here exercised at the workload/W fan-out key. The resync-side coalescing (the node/… key) is the sibling S-266-19 at 01-02 — the two keys never collide, so each coalescing path is pinned separately.

The interest table is built once at registration from AnyReconciler::interests(); the router's only effect universe is broker.submit((reconciler, target)); injected capability = a restricted EvaluationBroker handle (not a god-object). No warm cache; hydration per-tick (ADR-0036). No API beyond ADR-0081; the router mutation surface (RowKind → interested (reconciler, target_from) routing + derive_target) is diff-scoped-mutation covered.
